anya: FYI — nightly container build for the attention kernels failed during link in inference-builder:prod-2026-03. Error looks like a glibc/toolchain mismatch. Can someone take a look?

anya: Error excerpt:
```
/usr/bin/ld: /opt/inference/lib/libattn.a(kernel.o): undefined reference to `__memcpy_avx_erms'
/opt/inference/lib/libfoo.so: undefined symbol: memcpy@GLIBC_2.28
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

ben: I can repro locally in the same container. Happens at link time when building fused/paged kernels. If the kernel build fails the runtime falls back to the generic attention path — huge perf hit for long contexts. Repro steps I ran:
```bash
docker run -it inference-builder:prod-2026-03 /bin/bash
cd /src/attn-kernels && mkdir build && cd build
cmake .. -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && make -j8
```
The link error appears ~halfway through make.

mike: Observed perf regression in canary after the fallback happened. Microbench numbers (seq=4096, batch=1, model=redwood/long-attn-small):
- fused/paged kernel (optimized build): 3.1 ms/token
- generic kernel (fallback): 11.8 ms/token
Throughput down ~3.7x. Also seeing spikes in memcpy in profiling flamegraph which aligns with unknown symbol fallback.

carlos: My hunch: we're linking a static object built against a newer glibc/libstdc++ than the base container provides. Two immediate things to try: build attn kernels as shared libs with -fPIC, and pin the build toolchain in the container (gcc/g++ version). Add CMake option: `-DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON` and avoid static linking of thirdparty libs that pull newer symbols.

sara: Also worth noting that kernel selection heuristics amplified the user-visible regression: when the fused/paged kernel isn't available we pick the generic kernel but batching heuristic still assumes lower latency and queues more requests into a slow path, increasing p99. Short-term testing knob: add env var `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=pagged` to force selection for experiments. Long-term: adjust heuristic to prefer low-latency kernels only if they are actually present; fallback should reduce batch window to avoid queuing into slow path.

ben: Reproduced Carlos' mitigation: rebuilding with `-DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON` and gcc-11 inside the container produces a shared lib that links fine on the base image. Quick Dockerfile tweak that fixed my local run:
```dockerfile
FROM ubuntu:22.04
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential gcc-11 g++-11 cmake ninja-build
ENV CC=gcc-11 CXX=g++-11
WORKDIR /src/attn-kernels
# build steps...
```
Switching to ubuntu:22.04 also gives newer glibc so fewer surprises.

mike: For the perf side, I ran a profiler with the rebuilt kernels and confirmed fused/paged restores latency. Also noticed that when kernels are built with different align/flags we get slightly different KV cache alignment behavior — leads to extra memcpy when copying pages into the KV slots. That's probably due to our page allocator assuming 64-byte alignment while the kernel was compiled with different ABI packing. We should assert alignment in the kernel API boundary.

anya: Plan of action: (1) short-term: pin builder base image to ubuntu:22.04 and install gcc-11/g++-11 in CI; (2) add `-DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON` to kernel builds and avoid static linking against newer libs; (3) add a CI matrix test that runs a small fused/paged smoke test to detect link-time mismatches; (4) add an env var to force kernel selection for testing; (5) add a unit that asserts KV page alignment on kernel init. I'll open a PR with the Dockerfile + CMake change and the smoke test.

anya: PR opened: https://git.redwood/inference/PR-2897 — pins image, installs gcc-11, sets PIC, and adds small smoke check. Assigning to @carlos for the build flags review and @sara for kernel-selection heuristic changes.

carlos: Will review the build flags tonight. If we still see symbol version issues we can add a lightweight repro container job in the matrix that validates ld --no-as-needed output.

sara: I'll add the kernel-selection fallback guard and the `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL` knob ASAP.

anya: Marking this thread resolved for now — will reopen if CI still fails after #2897 merges. :white_check_mark:
